claim: A lab handbook is a flexible document that outlines the ethos of a research lab or group.
source: A lab handbook is a flexible document that outlines the ethos of a research lab or group.
evidence: This is a definitional statement provided in the abstract of the manuscript.

claim: A good handbook will outline the different roles within the lab, explain what is expected of all lab members, provide an overview of the culture the lab aims to create, and describe how the lab supports its members so that they can develop as researchers.
source: A good handbook will outline the different roles within the lab, explain what is expected of all lab members, provide an overview of the culture the lab aims to create, and describe how the lab supports its members so that they can develop as researchers.
evidence: This is a prescriptive statement about what constitutes a good handbook based on the authors' perspective.

claim: Many of the problems that happen in labs have their origins in a failure to clearly communicate the ethos of the lab.
source: Many of the problems that happen in labs have their origins in a failure to clearly communicate the ethos of the lab, including what is expected of lab members with regard to collegial behaviour and interactions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' analysis of common lab problems described in the manuscript.

claim: If the PI is not clear about their expectations in terms of working hours, a lab member may end up spending too much time in the lab and run the risk of burnout.
source: For example, if the PI is not clear about their expectations in terms of working hours, a lab member may end up spending too much time in the lab (and run the risk of burnout; Woolston, 2021), or they may adopt a schedule that isn't compatible with the way the rest of the lab works (which could lead to friction with the PI).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Woolston, 2021.

claim: Lab handbooks help to promote wellbeing by reducing anxiety and avoiding misunderstandings.
source: Lab handbooks also help to promote wellbeing: writing down the expectations for a lab helps to reduce anxiety and avoid misunderstandings.
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' reasoning about the benefits of lab handbooks.

claim: Some lab members may be more comfortable reading about certain topics, such as mental health, than discussing them in person.
source: Crucially, some lab members may be more comfortable reading about certain topics, such as mental health, than discussing them in person.
evidence: This is an inference about lab member preferences based on the authors' understanding.

claim: Only 41% of researchers surveyed thought that their leaders communicate clear expectations regarding behaviours and/or culture.
source: A recent survey of almost 4000 researchers found that only 41% of respondents thought that their "leaders communicate clear expectations regarding behaviours and/or culture" (Wellcome Trust, 2022), and an informal poll at our centre found unanimous support for handbooks from early-career researchers.
evidence: This claim is supported by data from a survey cited as Wellcome Trust, 2022.

claim: An informal poll at the authors' centre found unanimous support for handbooks from early-career researchers.
source: A recent survey of almost 4000 researchers found that only 41% of respondents thought that their "leaders communicate clear expectations regarding behaviours and/or culture" (Wellcome Trust, 2022), and an informal poll at our centre found unanimous support for handbooks from early-career researchers.
evidence: This claim is based on data from an informal poll conducted by the authors.

claim: If all lab members are involved in the creation of the handbook, it will create opportunities for discussions about topics that matter to them.
source: If all lab members are involved in the creation of the handbook, it will create opportunities for discussions about topics that matter to them.
evidence: This is an inference about the benefits of collaborative handbook creation.

claim: Being empowered in handbook creation can improve the job satisfaction and wellbeing of lab members.
source: Being empowered in this way can improve the job satisfaction and wellbeing of lab members.
evidence: This is an inference about the psychological benefits of empowerment in the handbook creation process.

claim: A lab handbook that lays out a supportive and positive culture can aid recruitment if some or all of it is made public.
source: Fourth, a lab handbook that lays out a supportive and positive culture can aid recruitment if some or all of it is made public.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential recruitment benefits of public lab handbooks.

claim: A lab should write its handbook collaboratively as a group, alongside the PI, rather than leaving it to one person to do all the writing.
source: We strongly recommend that a lab writes its handbook collaboratively as a group, alongside the PI, rather than leaving it to one person to do all the writing.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the authors' experience and reasoning.

claim: Writing as a group helps to achieve buy-in and fosters discussion.
source: In addition to sharing the workload, writing as a group helps to achieve buy-in and fosters discussion.
evidence: This is an inference about the benefits of collaborative writing based on the authors' experience.

claim: A short handbook that has been completed is better than a long handbook that has not.
source: Importantly, handbooks do not need to be long to be useful: a short handbook that has been completed is better than a long handbook that has not.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the authors' judgment about handbook creation.

claim: The Physics group at the Wellcome Centre for Integrative Neuroimaging (WIN) has around 30 members.
source: The Physics group at the Wellcome Centre for Integrative Neuroimaging (WIN) has around 30 members.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the size of the WIN Physics group.

claim: At the time the WIN Physics lab handbook was written, the group consisted of 4 PIs, 5 members of core staff, around 10 early-career researchers, and around 10 doctoral students.
source: At the time we wrote our lab handbook, the group consisted of 4 PIs (including KLM), 5 members of core staff, around 10 early-career researchers (including BCT), and around 10 doctoral students.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the composition of the WIN Physics group at a specific time.

claim: A group of about 15 volunteers within the WIN Physics group held a series of brainstorming sessions to decide what their handbook would contain.
source: A group of about 15 volunteers within the group held a series of brainstorming sessions to decide what our handbook would contain.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the handbook creation process.

claim: The WIN Physics group read example handbooks from other labs to help select high-level topics for their own handbook.
source: We also read example handbooks from other labs to help us select high-level topics for our own handbook, initially guided by a comprehensive Twitter thread from Sam Mehr of the University of Auckland (Mehr, 2019).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the handbook creation process, with a citation to Mehr, 2019.

claim: The WIN Physics group was initially guided by a comprehensive Twitter thread from Sam Mehr of the University of Auckland when selecting topics for their handbook.
source: We also read example handbooks from other labs to help us select high-level topics for our own handbook, initially guided by a comprehensive Twitter thread from Sam Mehr of the University of Auckland (Mehr, 2019).
evidence: This is a factual statement about a resource used in the handbook creation process, with a citation.

claim: The approach taken by the WIN Physics group to writing their handbook is outlined in Figure 1.
source: The approach we took to writing the handbook is outlined in Figure 1.
evidence: This statement refers to Figure 1 which shows the process of handbook creation.

claim: Writing a lab handbook as a collaborative group exercise helps to achieve buy-in and encourages discussion.
source: Writing a lab handbook as a collaborative group exercise helps to achieve buy-in and encourages discussion.
evidence: This claim appears in Figure 1 and is based on the authors' experience.

claim: The final WIN Physics lab handbook is split into three main sections: (i) the roles and expectations of different lab members; (ii) the group culture they aspire to create; (iii) their commitment to the development of lab members as researchers.
source: The final WIN Physics lab handbook is split into three main sections: (i) the roles and expectations of different lab members (including PIs, early-career researchers and doctoral students); (ii) the group culture we aspire to create (including workplace conduct, member wellbeing, good lab citizenship and equity, diversity and inclusion); (iii) our commitment to the development of lab members as researchers (including career development, best research practices, collaboration, travelling and public engagement).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the structure of the WIN Physics lab handbook.

claim: The writing process changed PIs' thinking in several cases.
source: In several cases, the writing process changed PIs' thinking.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the impact of the handbook creation process on PIs.

claim: One PI's statement 'I don't mind what hours you work as long as you are making progress' was interpreted in different ways by different members of the lab.
source: For example, it became clear during the process that one PI, intending to communicate the importance of a healthy work-life balance, would frame their expectations as "I don't mind what hours you work as long as you are making progress". However, it became clear during discussion that this statement was interpreted in different ways by different members of the lab: was it intended to support work-life balance, or to indirectly communicate that members of the lab are expected to work long hours?
evidence: This is a factual observation from the handbook creation process.

claim: The WIN Physics lab handbook now adopts more direct language about working hours and work-life balance, stating that they do not encourage long working hours.
source: As a result, we now adopt more direct language about working hours and work-life balance, stating that we do not encourage long working hours, and asking lab members to respect the working hours of colleagues.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the content of the WIN Physics lab handbook.

claim: The WIN Physics lab handbook explicitly states that members should not feel pressured to travel to conferences.
source: Our handbook now explicitly states that members should not feel pressured to travel, and to discuss mitigation options with their supervisor to ensure they do not miss out on career development opportunities.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the content of the WIN Physics lab handbook.

claim: The WIN Physics lab handbook has been well received by recent new starters.
source: The handbook has been well received by recent new starters, with one saying that they were surprised to see an explicit statement that long working hours are not expected.
evidence: This is a factual statement about feedback received on the handbook.

claim: One new starter was surprised to see an explicit statement in the WIN Physics lab handbook that long working hours are not expected.
source: The handbook has been well received by recent new starters, with one saying that they were surprised to see an explicit statement that long working hours are not expected.
evidence: This is a factual statement about specific feedback received on the handbook.

claim: The authors recommend writing the handbook over the course of a single term or semester.
source: Based on our experience, we would recommend writing the handbook over the course of a single term or semester, and the resources described in Box 1 should help with this.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the authors' experience.

claim: If the authors were to repeat the handbook creation process, they would lay the foundations of the handbook at a group 'away day', rather than having a number of short meetings over a period of several weeks.
source: Were we to repeat the process, we would lay the foundations of the handbook at a group 'away day', rather than having a number of short meetings over a period of several weeks.
evidence: This is a reflection on the handbook creation process based on the authors' experience.

claim: The WIN Physics group is a collaboration between three senior and four junior PIs, alongside five senior staff physicists.
source: Contrary to the traditional single-PI lab, the WIN Physics group is a collaboration between three senior and four junior PIs, alongside five senior staff physicists.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the structure of the WIN Physics group.

claim: The WIN Physics group opted for a joint handbook rather than individual handbooks for each PI because group members identify more strongly with the collective than their own supervisor.
source: While each PI could have authored their own handbook, we opted for a joint document, since our group members identify more strongly with the collective than their own supervisor and we have a strong sense of a shared group culture.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the decision-making process for the handbook.

claim: One downside of the joint handbook approach is that the handbook is less specific about topics where the PIs favoured different approaches.
source: The one downside of this joint approach is that the handbook is less specific about a number of topics where the PIs favoured different approaches (e.g., communication style or supervisory preferences).
evidence: This is a factual observation about a limitation of the joint handbook approach.

claim: The authors are now beginning to promote lab handbooks more broadly across Oxford University.
source: We are now beginning to promote lab handbooks more broadly across Oxford University.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the authors' current activities.

claim: The authors initially established a series of writing and discussion sessions to facilitate handbook creation, but found that most groups were content to work on their handbooks independently using their resources as a guide.
source: We initially established a series of writing and discussion sessions to facilitate this process, but found that most groups were content to work on their handbooks independently using our resources as a guide.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the authors' experience promoting lab handbooks.

claim: The authors have decided to make their lab handbook resources publicly available.
source: Based on this we have decided to make these resources publicly available (Box 1).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the authors' decision.

claim: The authors recommend striking a balance between writing a unique lab handbook, harvesting good text from other handbooks, and using standardised text to describe institutional policies.
source: Whilst a lab's handbook explicitly describes the culture and practices of that lab, we recommend striking a balance between writing your "own" lab handbook, harvesting good text from other handbooks to avoid reinventing the wheel, and using standardised text to describe institutional policies.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the authors' judgment.

claim: It is important that a lab handbook is consistent with and refers to other policies and documents in the host department and institution.
source: It is also important that a lab handbook is consistent with and refers to other policies and documents in the host department and institution (and also with relevant legislation).
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the authors' understanding of institutional requirements.

claim: A lab handbook is an essential resource for any lab.
source: We believe that a lab handbook is an essential resource for any lab, enabling it to operate with a healthy culture and to promote wellbeing amongst group members.
evidence: This is the authors' opinion based on their experience and reasoning.

claim: Making lab handbooks a common feature of research groups will help to increase job satisfaction, improve lab productivity, and contribute more broadly to positive research culture.
source: Making lab handbooks a common feature of research groups will, we believe, will help to increase job satisfaction, improve lab productivity, and contribute more broadly to positive research culture.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the potential benefits of widespread lab handbook adoption.

claim: Lab handbooks ensure that all lab members receive a consistent message and new starters feel welcome.
source: In addition to making sure that all lab members receive a consistent message and new starters feel welcome (Andreev et al., 2022), a good lab handbook will ensure the following:
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Andreev et al., 2022.

claim: A lab handbook enables a lab to operate with a healthy culture and to promote wellbeing amongst group members.
source: We believe that a lab handbook is an essential resource for any lab, enabling it to operate with a healthy culture and to promote wellbeing amongst group members.
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' reasoning about the benefits of lab handbooks.

claim: Articulating the ethos of a lab forces a research group to think more deliberately and strategically about how to create and communicate the culture they want to create and maintain.
source: It can be easy to allow practices and attitudes in the lab to evolve unchecked; however, if a research group has to articulate their vision for their lab in writing, it will force them to think more deliberately and strategically about how to create (and communicate) the culture they want to create and maintain.
evidence: This is an inference about the cognitive benefits of the handbook creation process.

claim: The act of writing a lab handbook can bring a lab together.
source: Third, the act of writing can bring a lab together.
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' experience with the handbook creation process.

claim: Co-creating a lab handbook can be a great way to demonstrate a commitment to positive research culture where funding bodies expect this.
source: While we would discourage groups from undertaking a lab handbook for cynical reasons, co-creating a lab handbook can also be a great way to demonstrate a commitment to positive research culture where funding bodies expect this.
evidence: This is an inference about the strategic benefits of lab handbooks in the context of funding.

claim: A lab handbook is not like a technical manual that explains how to perform a certain experiment or to use computing resources.
source: Crucially, a lab handbook is not like a technical manual that explains, for example, how to perform a certain experiment or to use computing resources (although such manuals are also valuable).
evidence: This is a definitional statement clarifying what a lab handbook is not.

claim: A good lab handbook will explain what is expected from lab members and the opportunities that are available to them.
source: A good lab handbook will explain what is expected from lab members and the opportunities that are available to them; it will cover all career stages and all job roles; it will describe the culture and atmosphere that the lab aspires to; and it will articulate how the lab supports the professional development of its members.
evidence: This is a prescriptive statement about what constitutes a good handbook.

claim: A good lab handbook will cover all career stages and all job roles.
source: A good lab handbook will explain what is expected from lab members and the opportunities that are available to them; it will cover all career stages and all job roles; it will describe the culture and atmosphere that the lab aspires to; and it will articulate how the lab supports the professional development of its members.
evidence: This is a prescriptive statement about what constitutes a good handbook.

claim: A good lab handbook will describe the culture and atmosphere that the lab aspires to.
source: A good lab handbook will explain what is expected from lab members and the opportunities that are available to them; it will cover all career stages and all job roles; it will describe the culture and atmosphere that the lab aspires to; and it will articulate how the lab supports the professional development of its members.
evidence: This is a prescriptive statement about what constitutes a good handbook.

claim: A good lab handbook will articulate how the lab supports the professional development of its members.
source: A good lab handbook will explain what is expected from lab members and the opportunities that are available to them; it will cover all career stages and all job roles; it will describe the culture and atmosphere that the lab aspires to; and it will articulate how the lab supports the professional development of its members.
evidence: This is a prescriptive statement about what constitutes a good handbook.
